title: Integrals & Antiderivatives
description: Antiderivatives, fundamental theorem, areas, substitution and integration by parts.
html:
∫ Integrals & Antiderivatives

1. Antiderivatives

$$F' = f, \qquad \int f(x)\,dx = F(x) + C$$

$$\int x^n\,dx = \tfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} \ (n \neq -1), \quad \int \tfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \ln|x|, \quad \int e^x\,dx = e^x, \quad \int \sin x = -\cos x, \quad \int \cos x = \sin x$$

Linear substitution: divide by the inner derivative $a$, e.g. $\int e^{3x}\,dx = \frac{e^{3x}}{3}$. Always check by differentiating.

2. Definite integral

$$\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a) = \Big[F(x)\Big]_a^b$$

  • Integral = oriented area (negative below the axis)
  • Area: split at the roots, add absolute values
  • Area between curves: $\int_a^b (f - g)\,dx$ with $f \ge g$

3. Techniques

Substitution

$$\int 2x\,e^{x^2}\,dx = e^{x^2} + C \quad (u = x^2)$$

For definite integrals substitute the limits too.

Integration by parts

$$\int u v'\,dx = uv - \int u'v\,dx, \qquad \int x e^x\,dx = e^x(x - 1) + C$$

Improper integrals

$\int_1^\infty x^{-p}\,dx$ converges exactly for $p > 1$.

4. Applications

$$s = \int v(t)\,dt, \qquad \bar{f} = \frac{1}{b - a}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$$
